topics.name: Imagining: If I were ..., I would ...
Comparisons: as ... as and degrees of comparison

options: If I am a king, I would build a big library.
If I were a king, I would build a big library.
If I were a king, I will build a big library.
questions.rule: To imagine something unreal, say If I were ..., I would ...

options: The lamps were as yellow as honey.
The lamps were as yellow than honey.
The lamps were so yellow as honey.
questions.rule: To show two things are equal, use as + adjective + as: as yellow as honey.

questions.rule: A noun (feathers) is described by an adjective: beautiful feathers, not an adverb.

options: playing

questions.rule: After will, use the base verb: will play.

options: widest
wider

questions.rule: Comparing two things with than needs the comparative: wide - wider - widest.

questions.after: the lord of this land, I would plant mango trees.
options: were
am
will be
questions.rule: With would in the result, the if-part uses were: If I were ...
An adjective comes before its noun: a golden car.

chat: Are you coming to the park this evening?
options: Yes, if it doesn't rain, I will come along.
Yes, if it won't rain, I will come along.
Yes, if it doesn't rain, I came along.
questions.rule: Type 1: if + simple present, will + base verb: if it doesn't rain, I will come along.

chat: Which is bigger, a tiger or a cat?
options: A tiger is much bigger than a cat.
A tiger is much more big than a cat.
A tiger is much biggest than a cat.
questions.rule: Short adjectives take -er: big - bigger. Never 'more big'.

questions.source: No other animal in the forest is as strong as the tiger.
options: The tiger is stronger than all animal in the forest.
The tiger is more stronger than any other animal in the forest.
The tiger is stronger than any other animal in the forest.
questions.rule: Positive to comparative: stronger than any other + singular noun.

options: If you will water the citron trees, they grow well.
If you water the citron trees, they will grows well.
If you water the citron trees, they will grow well.
questions.rule: Type 1: if + simple present, then will + base verb.

options: The music sounded sweetly in the evening.
The music sounded sweet in the evening.
The music sounded sweetness in the evening.
questions.rule: After sound, look, feel, taste, use an adjective: it sounded sweet.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: much
very
most

questions.rule: the ... I have ever seen needs the superlative: the most beautiful.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: fly
flying
flies

questions.rule: After would, use the base verb: would fly.

options: sweetly
sweeten
sweet
questions.rule: After was, describe the subject with an adjective: the music was sweet.

options: caught
will catch
would caught
questions.rule: Type 1: if + present (leave), result will + base verb (will catch).
Comparative + than: this valley is greener than that one.

chat: What would you do with a magic carpet?
options: If I had one, I would flew to the hills.
If I had one, I would fly to the hills.
If I had one, I will flying to the hills.
questions.rule: For an imagined situation: If + past (had), would + base verb (would fly).

questions.source: If you do not hurry, you will miss the school bus.
options: Unless you do not hurry, you will miss the school bus.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the school bus.
Unless you hurry, you missed the school bus.
questions.rule: Unless means 'if not', so drop the 'not': Unless you hurry, you will miss the school bus.

questions.source: The tiger is stronger than the deer.
options: The deer is not as strong as the tiger.
The deer is not as stronger as the tiger.
The deer is as strong as the tiger.
questions.rule: Comparative to positive: not as + adjective + as, and swap the two things: the deer is not as strong as the tiger.

options: Her rivers are the most beautiful in the land.
Her rivers are the beautifulest in the land.
Her rivers are the more beautiful in the land.
questions.rule: Long adjectives take the most in the superlative: the most beautiful.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct piece of advice.
options: If I were you, I would wear the green robe.
If I am you, I would wear the green robe.
If I were you, I would wore the green robe.
questions.rule: To give advice, say If I were you, I would + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: darkness
dark
darken

questions.rule: After looked (a linking verb), use adjectives: dark and quiet.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: waking
wake

questions.rule: After will, use the base verb: will wake up.

questions.rule: For more than two things, use the superlative: the greenest.
An imagined wish: would + verb ... if he were ...
Type 1: If + simple present, then will + base verb.

chat: How was your trip to the hills?
options: It was most exciting than our last trip.
It was more excitinger than our last trip.
It was more exciting than our last trip.
questions.rule: Long adjectives use more with than: more exciting than.

chat: How does your new flute sound?
options: It sounds really sweetly.
It sound really sweet.
It sounds really sweet.
questions.rule: It sounds (-s with 'it') + adjective sweet.

questions.source: Water the trees daily. They will grow fast.
options: If you water the trees daily, they grew fast.
If you will water the trees daily, they will grow fast.
If you water the trees daily, they will grow fast.
questions.rule: Type 1: the if-part takes the simple present, not 'will': If you water ...

options: It was the most beautiful evening of the year.
It was most beautiful evening of the year.
It was the more beautiful evening of the year.
questions.rule: A superlative needs the: the most beautiful evening of the year.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct sentence with a question tag.
options: If it rains, the picnic will be cancelled, will it?
If it will rain, the picnic will be cancelled, won't it?
If it rains, the picnic will be cancelled, won't it?
questions.rule: If-part in simple present. A positive sentence with will takes the tag won't it?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: grace
gracefulness
gracefully

questions.rule: To tell how the peacock danced, use an adverb: danced gracefully.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: call
calling
calls

questions.rule: After would, use the base verb: would call.

options: sweeter
the sweeter
the sweetest
questions.rule: ... I have ever tasted needs the superlative: the sweetest.

questions.after: the flute well at the school show.
options: played
will play
play
questions.rule: Type 1: if + present (practises), result will + base verb (will play).
Question word + would + subject + verb ... if she were ...?

chat: What did you see at the zoo?
options: We seen two beautiful white peacocks.
We saw two beautifuls white peacocks.
We saw two beautiful white peacocks.
questions.rule: Simple past of see is saw. Adjectives never take a plural -s: beautiful peacocks.

questions.source: Very few birds are as colourful as the peacock.
options: The peacock is one of the most colourful bird.
The peacock is one of the most colourful birds.
The peacock is the most colourful birds.
questions.rule: Very few ... as ... as becomes one of the most ... + plural noun (birds).

questions.source: Meera said, "I will plant citron trees."
options: Meera said that I would plant citron trees.
Meera said that she would plant citron trees.
Meera said that she will planted citron trees.
questions.rule: I becomes she, and will becomes would in reported speech.

options: If I were the Lord of Tartary, I would ride through the glades every morning.
If I were the Lord of Tartary, I will ride through the glades every morning.
If I were the Lord of Tartary, I would rode through the glades every morning.
questions.rule: If I were goes with would + base verb: would ride.

options: The night sky here is far more brighter than the sky in the city.
The night sky here is far brighter than the sky in the city.
The night sky here is far brightest than the sky in the city.
questions.rule: far can strengthen a comparative: far brighter. Never use 'more' with an -er word.

options: much

questions.rule: Of all the valleys = more than two, so use the superlative: the most peaceful.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: miss
missing

questions.rule: After will, use the base verb: will miss.

questions.after: that it looked like a sheet of glass.
options: calm
calmly
calmness
questions.rule: so + adjective + that: the lake was so calm that ...
Type 1: If + simple present (shine), will + base verb (will sleep).

questions.source: If the peacocks are not fed, they will fly away.
options: Unless the peacocks are not fed, they will fly away.
Unless the peacocks are fed, they would flew away.
Unless the peacocks are fed, they will fly away.
questions.rule: Unless already means 'if not', so remove 'not': Unless the peacocks are fed ...

chat: What would you do if you were a king for a day?
options: If I am a king for a day, I would opened free schools.
If I were a king for a day, I would open free schools.
If I were a king for a day, I will open free schools.
questions.rule: Answer the imagined question the same way: If I were ..., I would + base verb.

chat: Is the new trumpet louder than the old one?
options: Yes, it is much more louder than the old one.
Yes, it is much louder than the old one.
Yes, it is very louder than the old one.
questions.rule: Use much (not 'very') to strengthen a comparative: much louder.

questions.source: The peacock is the most beautiful bird in the court.
options: The peacock is more beautiful than any other bird in the court.
The peacock is more beautiful than any other birds in the court.
The peacock is most beautiful than any other bird in the court.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: more ... than any other + singular noun (bird).
